title: How to Know When the AI Boom Is About to Go Bust
subject: Funding gaps as a warning sign for the AI investment boom
summary: Jonathan Weil argues that the clearest warning of an AI bust would be major companies losing access to fresh capital before becoming self-sustaining. He cites Pets.com’s collapse in 2000 and Freddie Mac’s difficulty replenishing capital in 2007 as examples of financing constraints exposing fragile businesses. In his September 2026 assessment, postponed AI-related IPOs suggest nervousness but do not establish that funding is drying up, because private investment remains available. Continued backing for OpenAI also supports partners such as Oracle, whose borrowing and data-center spending depend on anticipated customer revenue. A funding shortfall at a major AI developer could therefore reverse momentum across the sector. However, private developers’ limited financial disclosure makes their resilience difficult to judge, and Weil offers neither a reliable timetable for a bust nor evidence that the decisive financing cutoff has already arrived.
